title: Clinical Approach to Chronic Enteropathy Using Capsule Endoscopy in Two Dogs
content: Chronic enteropathy (CE) in dogs presents with persistent symptoms, such as vomiting, diarrhea, weight loss, and changes in appetite. Traditional diagnostic methods, including blood tests, ultrasonography, and endoscopy, often fail to assess the entire small intestine accurately. Capsule endoscopy offers a noninvasive approach that enables comprehensive visualization of the gastrointestinal tract and enhances diagnostic accuracy. In Case 1, a 10-year-old Maltese patient with chronic diarrhea and significant weight loss underwent capsule endoscopy, which revealed severe lacteal dilation and moderate gastric erythema, leading to a diagnosis of severe intestinal lymphangiectasia and moderate enteritis. Despite initial corticosteroid therapy and dietary changes, the clinical improvement was limited. Case 2 involved an 11-year-old mixed-breed dog with chronic vomiting, anorexia, and weight loss. Capsule endoscopy revealed moderate gastric erythema, severe small intestinal irregularities, and jejunal bleeding, leading to a diagnosis of mild esophagitis, moderate gastritis, and severe inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) with hemorrhage. Treatment with a hypoallergenic diet, corticosteroids, and acid suppressants gradually relieved symptoms. Capsule endoscopy provided crucial diagnostic insights and guided the effective treatment in both cases, mainly when conventional methods were inconclusive. This report highlights the utility of capsule endoscopy as a valuable tool for managing chronic enteropathy in dogs.
